paper.title: Safety, Immunologic, and Clinical Activity of Durvalumab in Combination with Olaparib or Cediranib in Advanced Leiomyosarcoma: Results of the DAPPER Clinical Trial
paper.note: Main text paywalled and not available. Paper text = publisher supplementary files (Methods S1, Tables S1-S3, Figure S1) + capsule README/metadata. Claims that only the main text would state are grey.

claims.text: In the LMS cohort of DAPPER, radiomic (CT), microbiome and clinical features are correlated with each other; the capsule's correlation analysis quantifies these associations and corrects for multiple testing (FDR-BH).
A reduced feature set (10 radiomic principal components + microbiome relative abundances + clinical variables) is used for univariate Cox survival analysis of OS and PFS.
Univariate Cox models identify features associated with OS and PFS; p-values are FDR-adjusted across the tested features.
Immune/angiogenic transcriptomic signatures associated with OS in DAPPER LMS patients were evaluated in an independent TCGA LMS cohort (n = 104) by GSVA and log-rank test.
Best overall response (RECIST v1.1 and iRECIST) of LMS patients on DAPPER: 1 PR, 10 SD, 17 PD; clinical benefit 5/28 (18%).
claims.location: Supplementary Table S1; Supplementary Table S2

claims.text: The DAPPER LMS cohort is representative of the leiomyosarcoma population in age (median 54.5 y, range 39-75), uterine primary share (60%) and sex, but enrolled primarily white individuals (80%).
Microbiome taxa present in fewer than 40% of patients were excluded from correlation analyses to account for zero-inflation.
Radiomic features were reduced by unsupervised PCA from 973 candidate features to 10 components ranked by explained variance.

findings.evidence: Post-baseline covariates (deep_checks.py): Best.Response.RECISTv1, Gr1.Gr2.Toxicities, Gr3.Toxicities are measured during or after treatment but enter the survival models (surv_object_OS, surv_object_PFS) as baseline predictors. A patient must survive long enough to have a best response or a toxicity grade (immortal-time / outcome-dependent covariate), so their hazard ratios are biased toward benefit.
findings.question_for_authors: Were these covariates handled with a landmark analysis or as time-dependent covariates?

findings.evidence: Rmd outputs (deep_checks.py): os_results computed in chunk(s) 0verall-Survival but never printed or written; the knitted output (dp_survival.nb.html, results/dp_survival.nb.html) can only hold what is printed: pfs_results. The stored result for os_results is therefore not in the materials.
findings.question_for_authors: Can the os_results table be added to the stored output?

findings.evidence: [W4] Are cell line source, authentication, passage number and mycoplasma testing stated? -> not_reported. No blinding statement for the imaging or IHC scoring.
findings.question_for_authors: Are cell line source, authentication, passage number and mycoplasma testing stated?

findings.evidence: Column trace (deep_checks.py): data/results/reduced-feature-set.csv has 41 columns after the code's own drops (line 20: features <- features[-1]); the model formulas use 39. Never modelled: Age, Gender. Steps: line 21: covariates <- colnames(features); line 22: covariates <- covariates[-1]; line 40: univ_formulas <- sapply(covariates[2:length(covariates)], function(x) as.formula(paste('surv_object_OS~', x))). Outcomes: surv_object_OS, surv_object_PFS.
findings.question_for_authors: Were Age, Gender meant to be tested? The index steps skip them without comment.

findings.evidence: Claim 'Gr1/Gr2 toxicity grade is strongly associated with radiomic Component 2 (r=-0.74, FDR p=0.0012)' holds in 19% of 108 universes. Single changes that flip it: corr_method=spearman; corr_method=kendall; outlier=z3; outlier=z2.5; subset=uterine. [Yellow, not red (build_passport.py): the multiverse ran on our re-implementation of the authors' code (the reproduction gate recorded a port gap), so the fragility needs to be confirmed with the authors' own code.]
findings.question_for_authors: Was the result checked under corr_method=spearman; corr_method=kendall; outlier=z3; outlier=z2.5; subset=uterine?
